article title: Expression of the cytochrome P450s, CYP6P3 and CYP6M2 are significantly elevated in multiple pyrethroid resistant populations of Anopheles gambiae s.s. from Southern Benin and Nigeria
source notes: Fourth instar larvae and pupae were collected
site notes: Not Listed-Site is an agricultural site, located in south East Benin on the outskirts of porto-Novo the capital city of Benin. The farm is 20 hectares = 0.2 sq. km. Site is in swampy areas providing ideal environment for permanent breeding of mosquitoes. Could not get site from the geo-refs available, so used article map and encarta to get coords. (coords given in paper are 4.43, 2.64, which fall >200km off the coast of Benin. Paper probably meant to give coords of 6.43, 2.64, which fall in the position indicated in the map, and in the area of Porto-Novo, as indicated by Aka et al., 1999 (http://www.pathexo.fr/documents/articles-bull/1999/1999n3/T92-3-2017.pdf), so have used coords of 6.43, 2.64 (EH))
farming notes: they grow cabbages, carrots, lettuce etc.

larval notes: Fourth instar larvae and pupae were collected from the breeding pools

author: Bashir
article title: EFFICACY OF AGNIQUE® (MMF) MONOMOLECULAR SURFACE FILM AGAINST IMMATURE STAGES OF ANOPHELES ARABIENSIS PATTON AND CULEX SPP (DIPTERA: CULICIDAE) IN KHARTOUM, SUDAN
journal title: SOUTHEAST ASIAN J TROP MED PUBLIC HEALTH
site notes: Not Listed- site is located in the middle of sudan, at the junction of the White Nile & Blue Nile rivers. (am unable to find a location for Bahary. Google earth has a position for Alhalfaia Bahary, about 10km north of the centre of Khartoum (15.706, 32.543 in encarta), and source found which describes Bahary as one of the three towns comprising the city of Khartoum, the others being Omdurman and Khartoum (Habbani et al., 2006). Omdurman and Khartoum found in city in encarta, but the third town is called North Khartoum (15.637, 32.53 in encarta). Furthermore, map in paper (at small scale) puts coords at about 16.226, 33.846, where there appear to be very few settlements whatsoever. Therefore have been unable to find a location, and have left blank (EH))
season notes:
The state is a semi-desert area with 3 seasons; dry season, usually starts in March and ends in June with a mean temperature of 38ºC and a maximum peak of 45ºC in.The rainy season extends from July to October, with a mean annual rainfall of 150 mm, and a maximum peak of 200 mm in August, the temperature range is 28º-35ºC, with a relative humidity of 40-60%. The winter season starts in November and ends in February with average maximum and minimum temperatures of 25ºC
and 16ºC, respectively, and a relative humidity of 30-40%.
farming notes: Vegetables, animals fodder, wheat, maize, sorghum, millet, sweet potatoes, beans, onion, groundnuts and fruits are produced.
larval notes:
Agnique® MMF, (ISA-2OE, ethoxlated isostearyl alcohol) was tested for the control of An. arabiensis larvae in Bahary, Khartoum, Sudan. Each pond size was 50 cm x 50 cm x 35 cm. The ponds were flooded with well water on October 23 and by October 26 almost all the ponds became infested with anopheline and culicine larvae. Of the 10 ponds, 5 were treated with Agnique® and 5 served as untreated controls. The mean water temperature during the study period ranged from a low of
15.4ºC (8 to 26ºC) to high of 25.6ºC (15 to 34ºC) whereas the pH averaged 8.01 (7.8-8.2).

control notes: About 90% of households interviewed in Mwea division have bed nets, 65% of which are treated with insecticides other control methods iclude; environmental management that included removal of stagnant water bodies and removal of brush in the household compound. In addition, the respondents used several methods to lower the numbers of mosquitoes in their homes including mosquito repellants (31%), insecticides canisters (11%) bought from the shops, window and door screens (6%), traditional plants (3%) and ‘‘other methods’’ (3%). These ‘‘other methods’’ include burning herbs in their homes and avoiding construction of homes in swampy areas.
